stories.headline: Boehly, Walter sell Chelsea stakes as Clearlake takes full control
stories.summary: Clearlake Capital has taken full control of Chelsea after acquiring the ownership stakes of Mark Walter and Todd Boehly, the Premier League club announced Wednesday.
stories.body:
Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter have sold their stakes in Chelsea in a deal that gives Clearlake Capital full control of the English Premier League club.

Private equity firm Clearlake, led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano, previously owned a 61.5% stake in Chelsea, while U.S. businessmen Walter and Boehly each owned 12.83%. The club said in Wednesday's announcement that Swiss philanthropist Hansjörg Wyss, who also owned a 12.83% stake, will remain a partner in the ownership group.

The consortium bought Chelsea for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion) in 2022 with a further £1.75 billion ($2.3 billion) committed to investment in the club after former owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned by alleged ties to Russia president Vladimir Putin following the country's invasion of Ukraine.

The Financial Times reported that Warner and Boehly will receive £950 million ($1.3 billion) for their combined stake in a deal that values the club at £5 billion ($6.7 billion) including debt.

Boehly also held the position of club chairman, a role which he will now relinquish.

Chelsea said chairman Boehly had shown "unwavering commitment" to the ownership group's belief that the supporters are at the heart of the club.

"It has been an honour to serve as Chairman of Chelsea Football Club," Boehly said in a Chelsea statement. "I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the Club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

"I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the Club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake's leadership."

ESPN reported last month that the relationship between Clearlake and other investors, specifically Boehly, deteriorated over recent years with each looking to buy the other out in 2024.

Walter last month completed the sudden sale of the Los Angeles Lakers to venture capitalist Joshua Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger at a $12.5 billion valuation.

Walter, who only acquired the Lakers 14 months earlier, is under federal investigation relating to insurance companies he owns. He remains owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Chelsea, who appointed Xabi Alonso as manager in the summer and are currently sixth in the Premier League, said there will be no changes to day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the club.

Information from ESPN's James Olley and PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Buccaneers' Zampese says Browns messed up by trading Mayfield
stories.summary: Buccaneers assistant coach Ken Zampease, who was Baker Mayfield's QB coach with the Browns in 2018, says Cleveland messed up by trading the QB away.
stories.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Buccaneers senior offensive assistant/pass game specialist Ken Zampese was with quarterback Baker Mayfield just one year in Cleveland, but he saw enough then and now that has him convinced the Browns made a mistake trading him in 2022.

"They had the guy," Zampese, who was the Browns quarterbacks coach in 2018, told ESPN ahead of the teams' matchup Sunday in Tampa. "They had the guy and they gave him up."

Mayfield faced the Browns in Week 1 in 2022 with the Panthers, but Jacoby Brissett was Cleveland's starting quarterback as Deshaun Watson was serving an 11-game suspension. The Panthers lost 26-24. This time, it will be Watson on the other side of the ball.

"The year we were there, we were one of the best offenses in the NFL the second half of that season, 5-3, in a place that was -- before that season started -- 1-31," Zampese said of Mayfield. "The script got flipped and the city came alive because they finally drafted a quarterback that worked out for them and they mucked it up. They mucked it up."

When asked if he thinks the Browns share his sentiment, Zampese said, "Oh, I don't know. It doesn't matter. We got the guy we wanted [in Tampa] and that's what's important ..."

Mayfield went 29-30 as a starter with the Browns, leading them to the playoffs in 2020, where they clinched their first postseason victory in 26 years with a 48-37 win at the Steelers. He threw for 263 yards and three touchdowns in that performance before losing to the Chiefs 22-17 in the AFC divisional round.

That was the high point and what Mayfield has chosen to think about from his time in Cleveland.

"With any experience, there's ups and downs, good and bad," Mayfield said. "Ultimately, you remember the good more so than the bad - the first time having a playoff win since '94 there and going on the road and doing it in Pittsburgh. So it's a lot of good memories there. A lot of teammates that are friends for life."

But Mayfield struggled with injuries the following year in 2021, including a torn labrum in his non-throwing shoulder suffered in Week 2. He wore a harness to stabilize the joint, but then-offensive coordinator Alex Van Pelt said it impacted his throwing mechanics. He also navigated knee and foot injuries. On top of that, Mayfield faced death threats on social media, and public criticism from teammate Odell Beckham Jr.'s father.

Mayfield had also received criticism for some of the things he said publicly, such as calling former head coach Hue Jackson "fake." His brother Matthew had also taken to social media to express his own dissatisfaction with the Browns in 2018.

"Whenever a quarterback is drafted that high, everything's set up for you to fail. You haven't done this yet. You haven't accomplished this yet. I compared you with this guy in the history of the organization. I mean, goodness gracious," Zampese told ESPN.

In March of 2022 -- two months after undergoing shoulder surgery -- Mayfield learned through social media that the team was pursuing Watson in a trade with the Texans. He told ESPN's Adam Schefter at the time, "It's in the mutual interest of both sides for us to move on. The relationship is too far gone to mend. It's in the best interests of both sides to move on."

The Browns handed Watson a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract. In July 2022, they traded Mayfield to the Panthers for a conditional draft pick.

The Panthers released him in December of that year, and he had a brief stint with the Rams, where he "fell in love with football again," playing in Sean McVay's system. That's also where he met his eventual Bucs offensive coordinator Liam Coen -- now the head coach of the Jaguars -- and his current offensive coordinator in Tampa, Zac Robinson.

The Rams stint led to a one-year 'prove it' deal with the Bucs in 2023, culminating in an NFC South title that season and a wild-card playoff victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. He'd lead the Bucs to another division title in 2024. An injury-marred season for both Mayfield and the Bucs set them back in 2025, but he was rewarded with a three-year, $165 million contract extension.

"I think for me it goes back to the faith, looking up and knowing that no matter what happens, if I control what I can control, I'm doing things the right way," Mayfield said. "Obviously I want to win as an ultra-competitor, that's what you want to do at all times. So having trust in that, having faith in that and taking it one day at a time."

Mayfield told the "4th & South" podcast this summer that he's had this Week 2 game circled since the schedule came out.

But in Week 1, he fumbled the ball three times in a season-opening 33-27 loss at the Bengals. When the conversation in postgame quickly shifted to Cleveland, his response was more measured: "Obviously, there's history there -- there's no way to go around that," Mayfield said.

Much of his focus this week has been on the details of his performance rather than the opponent. Zampese believes that will help him manage his emotions, along with his ability to compartmentalize.

"Yeah, it's part of the job. And the guys that don't play the position very long, if you're ruled by your emotions that way, you're going to have a rollercoaster ride," Zampese said. "It's the ability to remove yourself from the ups and downs of that or just use it to provide energy and juice for the next situation to get into rather than thinking of the past and letting it bog you down ..."

Watson was suspended 11 games to begin the 2022 season and fined $5 million for violating the league's personal conduct policy after he was accused by more than two dozen women of sexual assault and sexual misconduct during massage therapy sessions. Two grand juries in Texas declined to pursue criminal charges against him.

In 2023, the Browns lost Watson to a season-ending shoulder injury in Week 10. In 2024, in Week 7, he suffered a torn Achilles tendon in his right leg, forcing him to undergo surgery and then a second surgery after re-rupturing it in January of 2025. He has gone 9-11 in just 20 games as the Browns' starter, including a 34-10 loss to the Jaguars last week in which he threw a touchdown and an interception and was sacked five times. It wasn't even certain that Watson would start in Week 2 until new head coach Todd Monken announced it this week.

Ironically, Monken was Mayfield's offensive coordinator in Cleveland in 2019. He believes he could have done a better job in guiding the Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback. They finished 6-10 that second season.

"I just know the competitor he is, and I've said it all along, I wish I had done a better job in '19," Monken said. "I've said that a lot of times. You've got to own the things you can be better at as a coach. And I'm sure there's certain things that, throughout the course of his life or career, he would look at the same way. Ultimately, I was not here for the rest of it, but I can just tell you that you want your players wired like Baker Mayfield."

Monken applauded Monken's play -- which he said has been at an "elite level," along with his competitiveness, and the way he has held himself to a high standard and others to a high standard, describing it as "everything you're looking for in a player ... just in a human being in general."

Mayfield acknowledged some of his own learning lessons from his time with the Browns, with a particular emphasis on his consistency as a leader.

"I think probably the biggest one -- trying to be the same person each and every day for the guys in the locker room, the people you work with, the staff that you're around each day, that some things are out of your control," Mayfield said. "If you're trying to get it fixed and you're not worried about the football aspects of your job, you're probably letting some things slide and fall by the wayside. So I think controlling who I am each and every day, trying to lead the best way possible and control the offense and ultimately win."

Zampese praised Mayfield as a leader and called last week's game a "blip on the radar" and said that there's an even more "heightened awareness" heading into this one, with better ball security, not trying to do too much.

"He's carrying all of us," Zampese said. "He just got rewarded for the job he's done and we all have great confidence in him doing an even better job as we move forward. And I know he does too."

ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes
stories.summary: Max Verstappen stormed through a field of 100 karters to win Max vs 100 in remarkable fashion as the four-time Formula 1 world champion made light work of the unique challenge at Silverstone.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen stormed through a field of 100 karters to win Max vs 100 in remarkable fashion as the four-time Formula 1 world champion made light work of the unique challenge at Silverstone.

Verstappen was given 30 laps, or 75 minutes, to overtake 100 drivers from the back of the grid in a go-kart race but only needed 13 laps, and 35 minutes, to add the latest win to his motorsport collection.

- As it happened: Relive Max vs 100 as Verstappen took on 10 karters

- HIGHLIGHTS: Watch the best bits from Max vs 100 on ESPN's YouTube

On a modified karting circuit at the home of F1 in the UK, Verstappen -- after starting 101st -- overtook 63 drivers on the very first lap, including ESPN's Nate Saunders, who barely lasted 10 seconds. Drivers clashed, spun around and ultimately watched Verstappen sail past as the predicted carnage ensued on Lap 1, resulting in waved yellow flags.

After that, Verstappen continued to carve his way through the field at an alarming rate, while also speaking to the competitors -- made up of athletes, content creators, journalists and other celebrities -- along the way.

"I'm coming for you," he said to a contestant at one stage. Later, he told commentators: "They need to focus because I'm definitely catching them."

It took Verstappen 15 minutes to get up to P7, and while at that stage he was still 14 seconds behind the runaway top three -- journalist Jacky Martens, YouTuber Zac Alsop and Red Bull's own Lewis Osler -- he quickly gained at a rate of around three seconds-a-lap.

The top three were given an extra 'fast lap' -- a shortcut of the circuit -- but that wasn't enough to catch Verstappen and he completed the challenge in style on Lap 13.

"My first lap was quite incredible," Verstappen said afterwards. "There was a lot happening and actually a few cars got stuck and I always managed to be on the other side, so didn't get stuck.

"And that made me get like 60 people in the first lap. So that just helps a lot, getting through to the front."

Asked where the win ranks in his victories, he said: "I think this is the best one yet!"

Saunders, meanwhile, was less positive post-race comments -- but nonetheless was impressed by the Dutchman.

"That was all a bit of a blur," he said. "Shortly after the start I looked to my right and there was Max -- and then he was gone. The way he was able to zigzag through the crowd was crazy."

The event was streamed live globally on ESPN on Disney+, while Verstappen will next be in action at F1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The Red Bull star is sixth in the drivers' championship.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Alexa Grasso shows off flyweight's elite status in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
It's uncommon for two fighters ranked in the pound-for-pound top 10 to meet in a bout with no championship at stake. But that was the case at Saturday's fourth annual Noche UFC, where Alexa Grasso faced Manon Fiorot.

Grasso is a former women's flyweight champion and Fiorot competed for the belt last year, so their status as MMA elites was well established before they fought. And when Grasso won by unanimous decision, she further solidified her standing in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

The top five of the rankings remains intact, and Grasso moves up from 10th to replace Fiorot at No. 6. Fiorot slips two positions to No. 8 in a pound-for-pound hierarchy in which seven of the 10 ranked women compete at flyweight (including Zhang Weili, the former UFC strawweight champion who last fought in an unsuccessful challenge of Valentina Shevchenko in November).

With Shevchenko injured and having vacated her title, there will be much scrambling for the top spot, which will be at stake when No. 5 Natalia Silva fights unranked Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 16. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

stories.headline: Cristian 'Kily' González arrives to take charge of Messi, Miami
stories.summary: New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.
stories.body:
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. -- New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.

González has now received the authorization to begin the job after being announced last month as the permanent replacement for interim coach Guillermo Hoyos on a contract through June 2028.

- Source: Colombia targeting U.S. U20 dual national Shaw

- Messi tracker: All goals, assists, key moments for Miami, Argentina in 2026

- Messi scores, but Nashville strikes late to deny Miami win

The job sees him reunite with Messi after the two shared the field for Argentina in two World Cup qualifiers in 2005.

"There are things in football that simply cannot be described in words; they are unique feelings. I feel privileged and blessed to have this opportunity and to share the fantastic relationship I have with Leo," González said in a news conference.

"I adore him, he knows it, and that makes this moment even more special. Being with him and sharing experiences with the incredible players on this squad. Honestly, as a coach, I feel completely fulfilled.

"Of course, this is all wonderful, but now we have to get to work. God willing, we'll start off strong tomorrow and win the championship."

González led his first training session with Inter Miami on Tuesday after landing in Miami from Argentina earlier in the morning. He will be on the sidelines for the team's Campeones Cup match against Liga MX champions Cruz Azul on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.

Inter Miami reached an agreement with González on Aug. 27, but the coach could not take over for Hoyos until receiving his work permit.

"What were these past few days like? To be honest, they were filled with a lot of anticipation. It had been nearly two and a half weeks and I couldn't be here, but this unique opportunity, something I hadn't even dared to dream of, became a reality," González said.

"We spoke with the club, and they offered me the chance to join the team; I said yes immediately. Being with the players, seeing their willingness to welcome my coaching staff, and watching them train the way they did today honestly, it made me very happy and gave me a huge boost of energy for tomorrow's match."

Miami's opponent in the Campeones Cup was delayed in arriving in Miami for the game and instead of landing in the U.S. on Monday, were unable to fly in until Tuesday.

"Well, more than an odyssey, sometimes accidents like this happen, and you just have to turn the page," said Cruz Azul manager Joel Huiqui. "The team is doing well. We rested very well yesterday, we stayed at a hotel in Mexico, and we're just arriving now. We're calm, obviously aware that tomorrow will be a huge match for us, and we're all focused.

"It goes without saying that [Messis] is a great player, but what matters most to me is that the team realizes what is at stake: not just another trophy, but our consolidation as an institution. Beyond the chance to face a great player, the opportunity to win the title against a team like Inter Miami is about solidifying the work we've been doing and, above all, bringing joy to the fans."

Inter Miami currently sits in second place on the Eastern Conference table with 45 points in 25 games. The team has recorded just one victory in its last nine games.

Inter Miami forward Luis Suárez said he wants to use the game against Cruz Azul to start strong under new leadership.

"When it comes to playing a match like this, it's a final. There is no time to dwell on the past, the only thing that matters is looking ahead to tomorrow," Suárez said. "We've come through a challenging run of games, but now we face the best possible scenario: playing a final and moving forward with a new coach who brings great positive energy, a strong desire to grow and plenty of enthusiasm.

"That attitude is contagious, and we are ready to support him and his coaching staff."

Inter Miami hosts Cruz Azul before returning to Major League Soccer regular season action on Sunday against San Diego.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail semifinals: Mulitalo relishing rematch, Katoa on possible Sharks curtain call
stories.summary: Ronaldo Mulitalo is determined to honour his departing Sharks teammates, Sione Katoa has opened up about his future at the Cowboys and his finals days at the Sharks, while Nathan Cleary is fighting the clock to be fit for Penrith's prelim.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's semifinal week.

Mulitalo relishing 'Marky Mark' rematch

Ronaldo Mulitalo is embracing another blockbuster battle with Roosters star Mark Nawaqanitawase, describing the departing winger as a "generational talent".

Mulitalo said Nawaqanitawase "brings the best out of me" and revealed their on-field rivalry is largely one-sided when it comes to the verbal exchanges.

"He's a gentleman out there... he doesn't really say anything. I think it's more myself," Mulitalo joked. "He knows I'm just going to keep talking, so he just ignores me anyway."

Mulitalo determined to honour departing Sharks

Ronaldo Mulitalo says Cronulla's finals run carries added significance with several longtime teammates set to leave the club at season's end.

Mulitalo said he has played alongside some of the departing Sharks since he was 16 and wants to "honour those boys" with his performance against the Roosters.

"I don't want to let them down and disappoint them, winning the game is the most important part of the week for me."

Katoa reveals Cowboys appeal

Sione Katoa has revealed North Queensland's attacking style was a major attraction behind his move to the Cowboys in 2027.

After helping eliminate his future club from the finals, Katoa told ESPN he "loves the style of footy" they play, describing it as "free footy" and similar to Cronulla's attack.

Katoa emotional over Sharks farewell
He also admitted the reality that every game could be his last for Cronulla is beginning to sink in.

"Tonight might have been the last week, maybe the last game," he told ESPN after scoring a double against North Queensland.

"I'm very happy right now that I get another week with my brothers and play again."

Cleary racing clock for preliminary final

Nathan Cleary is in doubt for Penrith's preliminary final after scans revealed an stress-related bone issue in his foot.

The Panthers will assess and monitor their star halfback over the next fortnight, with their week off providing valuable recovery time.

Cleary has, however, been cleared of any suspension concern after receiving only a Grade 1 Dangerous Contact charge for his incident with Hugo Savala.

stories.headline: Michael Carrick: 'We can't accept' Man United showing in Carabao Cup exit, 'I take responsibility'
stories.summary: Michael Carrick branded Manchester United's capitulation as unacceptable, after watching his team lose 3-2 to Brighton in the Carabao Cup after leading 2-0.
stories.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Michael Carrick branded Manchester United's capitulation as unacceptable, after watching his team lose 3-2 to Brighton in the Carabao Cup after leading 2-0.

United were dumped out despite goals from 19-year-old Shea Lacey and Mason Mount in the opening 10 minutes on Wednesday.

Fabian Hürzeler's side battled back thanks to goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper to win at Old Trafford for the fifth time in their last six visits.

"We can't accept that as a group," Carrick said.

"I take responsibility for it. The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me.

"We'll all be better. We have to be better. We're out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches. It doesn't feel good at the moment. It doesn't feel good.

"We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That's all I'm thinking about right now."

United have now won just two of their six games in all competitions to start the season and sit 13th in the Premier League table with four points.

The players were booed off following the defeat to Brighton, but Carrick rejected the suggestion his position could already be under threat.

"I don't feel under pressure," he said.

"Either way, that doesn't bother me one bit. It generally doesn't bother me one bit.

"I understand what goes on outside and how the world works, but it doesn't bother me. What bothers me is winning games and having a good feeling around the place.

"We've got to win football matches and we can do. I fully believe we will do. But obviously we've got to do it pretty quick and Sunday [against Fulham] is a starting point."

stories.headline: 49ers' De'Zhaun Stribling has surgery, to miss about 10 weeks
stories.summary: 49ers receiver De'Zhaun Stribling had surgery on his ankle and is expected to miss about 10 weeks, while tight end Jake Tonges has been ruled out for the season.
stories.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling had surgery on his ankle and is expected to miss about 10 weeks, coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday.

Stribling will be placed on injured reserve this week and the hope, Shanahan said, is that Stribling will be back this year.

"We feel good he'll get back this season," said Shanahan, who spoke to media for the first time since the team returned from Melbourne, Australia. "It'll take some time."

Tight end Jake Tonges, who will require surgery on the injured medial collateral ligament in his right knee, was put on injured reserve Wednesday and is out for the season, Shanahan said.

In related moves, the Niners promoted veteran wideout KhaDarel Hodge and tight end Brayden Willis from the practice squad to the 53-man roster.

Stribling sprained the deltoid ligament in his left ankle, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. He sought multiple opinions to potentially rest the ankle and come back to play but ultimately decided on surgery.

Shanahan said Stribling initially injured the ankle late in the first quarter on a pass play that went to tight end Luke Farrell. On the play, Stribling fell awkwardly on the ankle after he was hit by a Rams defender, hobbled to the sideline and went into the blue medical tent.

From there, Niners medical personnel checked to make sure his Achilles was intact and ruled out any issues there as well as any fear of a high ankle sprain. Stribling did some light jogging and running on the sideline before going back in the game in the second quarter.

Stribling ran a deep route and cut to his left before going down without contact.

"We were testing him," Shanahan said. "His Achilles [was] intact. We've seen it's not a high ankle sprain. He's running. We're going to let him go back in. And then he goes back in and does a turn that you don't replicate on the sideline, and then you find out it's worse than that."

With Stribling out, the Niners will be without two of their projected top three receivers for the bulk of the season. Ricky Pearsall landed on injured reserve during training camp with persistent knee issues and will not return this year.

The Niners now will lean on veterans Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson to handle the receiving load. Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and Hodge offer depth, and veteran Christian Kirk is eligible to come off injured reserve after Week 4.

Shanahan said he "believes" Kirk is on track to return at that time but added he's "not sure" about Kirk's status.

Regardless, Shanahan offered a vote of confidence for the receivers remaining on the roster.

"We have enough," Shanahan said. "It's always tough when you lose two of your main guys, but I think we have as good a depth as anyone in the league. It's fortunate that he's not gone for the year like Ricky. We will get him back, but we have the people to still hold it down while he's gone."

stories.headline: Max Scherzer gets win as Blue Jays beat Tigers 5-1 to avoid sweep, end Detroit's winning streak at 6
stories.summary: — Myles Straw had two hits and an RBI, Max Scherzer allowed one run in five innings for his second win in four starts and the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Tigers 5-1 on Wednesday afternoon, ending Detroit’s winning streak at six.
stories.body:
TORONTO -- — Myles Straw had two hits and an RBI, Max Scherzer allowed one run in five innings for his second win in four starts and the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Tigers 5-1 on Wednesday afternoon, ending Detroit’s winning streak at six.


The Blue Jays are 45-15 when they score five or more runs.


Brett Bateman had two hits and scored a run as Toronto avoided a three-game sweep and ensured it would not lose ground in the AL wild-card race. The Blue Jays (76-77) are 1 1/2 games behind the White Sox for the final postseason spot.


Chicago dropped into the wild-card position after losing 6-3 at Cleveland as the Guardians replaced the White Sox atop the AL Central.


Scherzer (3-8) allowed three hits, walked three and struck out three.


Blue Jays closer Louis Varland came on with runners at first and second in the ninth and wrapped it up for his 34th save in 36 chances.


Detroit’s Riley Greene hit an RBI single in the first inning but the Blue Jays answered with two in the fourth, chasing Tigers starter Keider Montero. Ernie Clement hit a sacrifice fly and Straw added an RBI single.


Montero (9-9) allowed two runs and six hits in four innings.


George Springer singled home a run in the fifth, and the Blue Jays took advantage of errors on three consecutive plays to score two more in the sixth.


Up next
Tigers: LHP Framber Valdez (10-10, 4.01 ERA) is scheduled to start at Chicago on Thursday against White Sox RHP Erick Fedde (8-9, 3.97).


Blue Jays: RHP Dylan Cease (11-5, 2.38) is expected to start at Texas on Friday. The Rangers had not named a starter.

stories.headline: Sources: Jessica Campbell, Bryan McCabe latest to join Devils
stories.summary: The Devils are hiring former Kraken assistant coach Jessica Campbell as manager of player development and longtime Panthers executive Bryan McCabe as vice president of prospect personnel, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
The New Jersey Devils are hiring former Seattle Kraken assistant coach Jessica Campbell as manager of player development and longtime Florida Panthers executive Bryan McCabe as vice president of prospect personnel, sources told ESPN.

Campbell, 34, became the first woman to serve as a full-time coach behind an NHL bench. She was promoted to Seattle in 2024 after helping the AHL's Coachella Valley Firebirds reach back-to-back Calder Cup Finals.

After her playing career, Campbell became a power skating and skills coach, working privately with NHL players before coaching professionally in Sweden and Germany.

McCabe, 51, will also serve as an assistant general manager for the Devils' AHL affiliate in Utica. He spent 14 years in the Panthers' front office, specializing in player development and personnel.

A longtime NHL defenseman, McCabe played 1,135 games and served as Panthers captain before moving into management. He was part of Florida's back-to-back Stanley Cup championships before leaving this summer when his contract expired.

McCabe is the third former Panthers executive to join Sunny Mehta in New Jersey. Mehta spent six seasons in Florida's front office before being named Devils GM in April. He has also hired former Panthers executive Braden Birch as assistant GM and Leo Luongo as director of goaltending.

stories.headline: UFC's Islam Makhachev questions validity of Jon Jones' wins streak
stories.summary: UFC champ Islam Makhachev believes Jon Jones' failed drug tests and issues outside the Octagon invalidate Jones' place among the UFC's all-time streaks for consecutive wins.
stories.body:
Jon Jones and Islam Makhachev, two of the greatest fighters in UFC history, are taking shots at each other this week.

Makhachev (29-1) broke the UFC's official win streak record in August, when he defended his welterweight championship against Ian Machado Garry for his 17th consecutive win. Former middleweight champion Anderson Silva held the previous record of 16. Jones, a former light heavyweight and heavyweight champion, would argue he won 20 bouts in a row from 2010 to 2024, but his streak was interrupted by a no-contest against Daniel Cormier in 2017.

In a recent interview with a Russian news outlet, Makhachev said Jones' no-contest, which was the result of a failed drug test by the United States Anti-Doping Agency, invalidates his win streak.

"I'm not denying that Jon Jones is one of the greatest athletes in history, but he was caught doping twice," Makhachev told Ushatayka. "I think that's why his streak isn't considered valid. Because he went into a fight while on PEDs and won, that's where a new count should have started."

Jonse (28-1) was fined and suspended 15 months for testing positive for extremely trace amounts of steroid metabolites. He initially defeated Cormier in their fight in 2017, before it was later changed to a no-contest.

An independent arbitrator later stated he believed Jones unknowingly ingested the substance and that it was not performance enhancing. Jones has long pointed to that independent finding as validation of his innocence, and did so again Monday in a post directed at Makhachev.

"If you believe USADA for finding a picogram in my system, then you must believe USADA when they say it 'It was not found to be PERFORMANCE ENHANCING or INTENTIONAL,'" Jones wrote on X. "You can't have it both ways. Last I checked, my hand got raised every time I was in the Octagon since any of you can remember. Your own coach said I was 'a gift from God.' Let's not forget you've been KO'd, flatlined, went night night."

Makhachev, whose only loss came by knockout to Adriano Martins in his second UFC fight in 2015, responded to Jones the following day, and hinted at Jones's troubled legal history, both in and out of competition.

"Jon, I'm not trying to diminish your achievements in any way," Makhachev wrote on X. "But your whole life seems to be tied to breaking the rules one way or another, and somehow, you're never the one to be blamed."

stories.headline: September Draft Power Rankings: An extended top 35, plus current player comparisons
stories.summary: The majority of top-age junior campaigns are now over, with prospects putting their best foot forward to show off for recruiters all season. Here's Jasper Chellappah's September Power Rankings, with an extended top 35 and player comparisons.
stories.body:
The majority of top-age campaigns are over, with prospects putting their best foot forward to show off for recruiters all season. Through club and state we've witnessed a draft class explode with depth across the year. 2026 offers a pool that runs 70 deep which clubs will be keen to take on in the national draft.

Jackson Phillips' Dandenong Stingrays will face Wil Malady's Gippsland Power in a south-west Victorian clash to decide the Coates Talent League premier. In WA, Heath Mellody and George Gale are into a WAFL Grand Final for Claremont against Peel.

Mellody headlines the movement in September's Power Rankings. His rise has come off the back of a brilliant stint at senior level after winning the Larke Medal at the National Championships. While not the favourite to be crowned pick one in the open draft he's amongst six named to still be in the most wide open race since Essendon last picked at the top in 2016.

With added player comparisons targeting the best traits of this year's prospects, this is ESPN's extended top 35 prospects in September for the AFL Draft.

Previous rankings: April | May | June | July | August | September

1. Dougie Cochrane (Port Adelaide NGA) (previously: 1)

Central District/South Australia

FWD/MID, 195cm

SANFL: 4 games, 17.8 disposals, 3.8 marks, 2.3 tackles

There was every chance Cochrane wouldn't play a game in his top-age season after undergoing patella surgery in the off-season. Instead we got to see him in a variety of roles for Port Adelaide's SANFL side late in the year with the athletic utility offering glimpses of class. He's been the 'pick 1 apparent' of his draft class since commanding performances at the U16s championships, backing it up with dominance beyond his years as a bottom-ager for club and state. Cochrane projects to become a key forward at the next level but holds ambitions of moving on-ball at 195cm. With Zak Butters pledging his future to the Western Bulldogs, Cochrane is all but assured of landing at Alberton.

Traits similar to: Charlie Curnow

2. Cody Walker (Carlton Father-son) (2)

Bendigo Pioneers/Vic Country

MID, 184cm

National Championships: 3 games, 23.7 disposals, 3.7 clearances, 1.3 tackles

Walker's stints with Carlton VFL cemented his status in this draft pool. He's an athletic talent around the ball with speed and balance allowing him to shark loose balls on the fly and exit the contest shoulders out and toward goal. Walker's kryptonite has continually been the ball use and decision making, often biting off too much or scrubbing kicks under pressure which puts his side on the back foot. There will be positional versatility in his game given the ball-winning quality and athletic tools, and he may need to hone his skills on the outside of the contest before graduating on-ball for the Blues.

Traits similar to: Chad Warner

3. Arki Butler (4)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID/FWD, 182cm

National Championships: 3 games, 12.3 disposals, 7.0 marks, 1.7 goals

Adversity hit Butler's airborne campaign with a broken collarbone during the National Championships. It put serious doubt into the remainder of his season but the goalsneak returned to captain Brighton Grammar to the first APS Grand Final win ever and put together an encouraging game on the weekend despite the Dragons losing out in a thrilling preliminary final. Butler has offered glimpses as a midfielder with his strength and acceleration -- attributes he can use to win his own ball, but he clearly projects as a powerful one-on-one goalkicker inside 50. The powerfully built teen is brilliant in the air, crafty at ground level and uses both feet around goals to pay full price. In a wide open race for the open pool No. 1 selection, Butler has his nose in front of a group of six.

Traits similar to: Toby Greene

READ: 'All damage' - Arki Butler is the 2026 draft's most watchable junior footballer

4. Heath Mellody (8)

Claremont/Western Australia

MID/DEF, 184cm

National Championships: 4 games, 28.2 disposals, 5.0 marks, 2.5 tackles

Mellody has been on the scene for 12 months. He ripped apart a Colts Grand Final from the wing as a bottom-ager and now gets his chance at a senior premiership with Claremont after a sparkling finish to his junior career. Mellody's second half of the season has been the best of anyone in the draft; the Larke Medallist was a shining light through the midfield for WA and didn't play a single Colts game before making his League debut in the final two rounds of the year.

Mellody has been a key piece of Claremont's run. He's been thrown around the ground including stints at half forward, halfback and on a wing, but his best football has come as a true centre bounce midfielder. He possesses an insatiable work ethic, hitting top speed to find space and commanding the football with his dogged determination to provide an option. He can win his own ball with clean hands under pressure but is at his best on the fly with eyes scanning inside 50. Mellody's ball use can be wayward as he tries to do too much at times, but he offers lovely technique and it has been a strength of his through junior football before his move into the midfield. He plays above his size with strong hands in the air which we saw off halfback last year and can get forward to hit the scoreboard bursting inside 50. This six-game stretch at senior level after winning the Larke Medal will see Mellody drafted as the highest WA prospect since Luke Jackson, and could even see him taken as the top pick in the open pool. He is 2026's draft bolter and could rise all the way to the pinnacle this year.

Traits similar to: Lachie Ash

THE PICK 1 PIE: Who is in the running to be taken first from the open pool?

5. Harry Van Hattum (3)

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

RUC/FWD, 205cm

National Championships: 4 games, 10.8 disposals, 2.5 marks, 22.0 hitouts

Few rucks possess the combination of traits Van Hattum is blessed with. A genuine ruck size with a top-heavy frame relied upon for his aggressive nature, the Knights star is an elite kick and strong presence at stoppages. If he isn't claiming the ball from ruck contests himself he's buttering up with craft in the clinches, getting on the burst to receive handballs and executing with ball use inside 50. He can get his contested marking game going around the ground and offers genuine presence as a target inside 50. Van Hattum's limitations come in his consistent efforts and fitness to spread from contests and run out games. He is clearly hampered by his tank and will need to become a strong runner in time to make it as an AFL ruckman because it doesn't come naturally to him.

Traits similar to: Brodie Grundy

READ: 'I just hate that' - Harry Van Hattum wants to end ruck disrespect

6. Ethan Drever (6)

GWV Rebels/Vic Country

MID, 188cm

National Championships: 4 games, 20.0 disposals, 4.5 marks, 4.2 tackles

No one stops Drever on the burst out of a contest. The flying Rebel is at his very best on the move around stoppage, collecting loose balls and creating separation with a long striding gait entering the 50. He's an excellent defensive presence at stoppage, willing to dig in to chase down opponents, apply physical pressure at the drop of the ball and run hard in defensive transition. That separates him from a lot of the very best midfielders to come through the junior pathways. Drever's consistency has been a point of contention for draft watchers, fluctuating in both his impact on the game and his skill execution by foot. He can be haphazard in his ball use forward of centre which holds Drever back from being the most damaging player in the pool.

Traits similar to: Finn Callaghan

7. Gus Teixeira (5)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 181cm

National Championships: 4 games, 17.0 disposals, 4.2 tackles, 1.8 goals

Teixeira plays with authority. The Dragons star has split time through the midfield and up forward through a breakout top-age season, but there remain doubts over whether he cracks it as an inside midfielder at the senior level. Teixeira is powerful with ball in hand, creates space for himself efficiently and executes well by hand and foot. He's a threat around goals and has the speed to play off half forward at the next level, but doesn't play through contact well and isn't the cleanest player in the draft below his knees. He projects to become an excellent forward that can pinch hit through the middle but may lack the natural midfield craft to operate in the engine room full-time.

Traits similar to: Jordan De Goey

8. Mitch Harris (12)

Woodville-West Torrens/South Australia

DEF, 195cm

National Championships: 4 games, 8.8 disposals, 3.5 marks, 1.0 tackles

There isn't a more intimidating aerial presence in the draft than Harris. A genuine contested marking threat at either end of the ground, he's honed his craft down back as a lockdown option and produced a stellar carnival to stake his claims as a top 10 pick. Harris does his work early and establishes position with his physicality, but also has a good vertical leap to come over the top of packs. He's offered glimpses of upside as a forward but will be drafted as a lockdown key defender.

Traits similar to: Sam Collins

9. Ethan Matthews (Giants Academy) (9)

Giants Academy/Allies

MID, 186cm

National Championships: 2 games, 25.0 disposals, 5.0 marks, 6.0 tackles

Matthews is an excellent midfield prospect that will find his way to the Giants via their academy. He's a ball magnet, clean and clinical with his use but not as damaging as others at the top of the pool in his willingness to take the game on and exit stoppage forward of centre. There's scope for Matthews to play through the midfield, off a wing or on halfback with his cleanliness, running power and reliability.

Traits similar to: Sam Flanders

10. Wil Malady (10)

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

FWD, 190cm

National Championships: 3 games, 10.7 disposals, 5.7 marks, 1.3 goals

Malady is one of the best athletes this year, a powerful runner with high top-end speed mixed in with a ridiculous vertical leap. His spring gives him a chance to fly for every ball kicked his way and his dogged running patterns put him in the best position to impact ahead of the ball. It's an unsexy pick to target third tall forwards at this stage of the draft but Malady offers match-winning traits with reliability in his role at the next level.

Traits similar to: Ollie Henry

11. Clancy Snell (7)

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

DEF, 196cm

National Championships: 4 games, 13.0 disposals, 7.0 marks, 2.5 tackles

Snell reads the play superbly and backs himself always. He's an interceptor first and foremost, relying on his superior reach, closing speed and reading of the ball in flight to pluck marks and kickstart transition. He can give up a long leash on direct opponents and get caught out by quick ball movement, but he's also shown off strong one-on-one play that gives scope for him to be a reliable lockdown defender in time.

Traits similar to: Josh Worrell

12. Khaled El Souki (Western Bulldogs NGA) (11)

FWD, 174cm

National Championships: 1 game, 10.0 disposals, 5.0 tackles, 1.0 goals

El Souki may be the hardest player to tackle in the draft. With his short stature, power through the hips and willingness to twist and turn out of danger, the Jets forward has been a goalkicking machine all season and gives defenders headaches with his activity around the ball. He's elite in forward stoppages with craft and confidence, and has shown glimpses of genuine midfield minutes if he can build his tank.

Traits similar to: Kysaiah Pickett

13. Sam Gayfer (13)

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

FWD, 194cm

National Championships: 4 games, 11.0 disposals, 4.2 marks, 2.5 goals

The vertical leap and aggression of Gayfer through the air is a joy to watch, crashing packs and exerting his presence consistently through games. His big carnival vaulted him up the rankings but he's also a willing defensive presence with the speed and aggression to chase down opponents. At the very minimum Gayfer will be an excellent role player with his capacity to bring the ball to ground and impact at his size.

Traits similar to: Mitch Georgiades

14. Leo Steed (17)

Swan Districts/Western Australia

MID, 176cm

National Championships: 4 games, 23.5 disposals, 3.0 marks, 4.0 tackles

Steed will be a fan favourite at the next level with a bucket of courage and bravery as a smaller midfielder. He accepts contact and plays through physicality, working himself into the ground to win his own ball and get it going forward. He's become a much better kick this year and, while still not a strength, found a role at senior level by hitting the scoreboard and setting up teammates inside 50. There's traits that will allow Steed to thrive as a midfielder at the next level if he can overcome middling athleticism.

Traits similar to: Caleb Serong

15. Jake Eime (18)

Central District/South Australia

DEF, 182cm

National Championships: 4 games, 20.2 disposals, 3.8 marks, 1.2 tackles

As a pure role player, there are few better halfback prospects to come through the junior ranks in some years. Eime is an elite athlete with the confidence to take the game on. He thrives in transition where he can motor along a wing and link the chains, though often will take on the riskier kick and back himself to execute, sometimes to the detriment of the team. Eime has the chops to lockdown on smalls, can play above his size in the air and loves to get forward and be damaging.

Traits similar to: Darcy Wilmot

16. Harrison Chapman (14)

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID, 190cm

National Championships: 3 games, 18.7 disposals, 4.7 marks, 2.0 tackles

There's something to unlock in Chapman's game at the next level. With his height and length he shouldn't be as natural below his knees and with ball in hand, expertly crafting attacking forays through the middle of the ground with multiple disposals in passages. He's a lovely quick and truly elite runner which gives him a chance of being an excellent wing at the next level, but it's the inside midfield upside that has clubs keen in the first round.

Traits similar to: Will Day

17. Caylen Murray (Lions Academy) (19)

Lions Academy/Allies

DEF/MID, 183cm

National Championships: 4 games, 24.0 disposals, 6.8 marks, 1.8 tackles

Murray is another in the line of excellent Lions academy prospects. One of the best ball users in the draft, he's willing to take on the kicks through the corridor but is equally adept at retaining possession and moving the ball methodically. Murray hasn't quite proved his midfield credentials but will become a reliable halfback quickly.

Traits similar to: Lachie Whitfield

18. Ethan Herbert (15)

North Adelaide/South Australia

RUC/FWD, 200cm

National Championships: 4 games, 15.8 disposals, 3.0 marks, 2.5 tackles

Herbert is a rare ruck archetype, with elite stoppage craft and the aerobic capacity to work opponents into the ground and win the ball on the outside. He's been a work in progress as a forward and some recruiters suggest he may be better suited to a key defence post where he can intercept, but there's untapped potential in what Herbert can produce at a genuine ruck size.

Traits similar to: Tim English

19. Kodah Edwards (16)

South Adelaide/South Australia

MID, 183cm

National Championships: 4 games, 22.0 disposals, 4.5 marks, 3.2 tackles

Edwards is unique in this draft. He's an inside midfielder in the older fashion of tough, bullocking prospects. But he's also got an X-factor to his game in the forward 50, thriving in one-on-ones and kicking goals by the bunch if given open space to work with. His limitations include ball use and decision making but his excellent hands and upside as a forward target gives him a chance of landing in the first round.

Traits similar to: Matt Kennedy

20. Tyson Bradley (20)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

DEF, 195cm

National Championships: 4 games, 14.5 disposals, 6.5 marks, 1.0 tackles

Bradley is the third of a group of key defenders who could land in the first round. The Vic Metro MVP and captain of the Sandringham Dragons is a neat ball user and can act as a distributor out of defence, plus reads the play well to operate as a sweeper behind the ball. Bradley ticks a lot of boxes for clubs in the market for a key defender around this point of the draft.

Traits similar to: Jordan Ridley

21. Noah Williams (21)

Geelong Falcons/Vic Country

MID, 177cm

National Championships: 4 games, 15.5 disposals, 4.0 marks, 5.8 tackles

There's no questioning Williams' endeavour and desperation. He's a maniacal presence at the coalface and looks at home on-ball since a move from halfback in the pre-season. Unfortunately it's been a season full of niggles and inconsistencies, and recruiters don't see the weapons that other midfielders possess at the top of the pool.

Traits similar to: Tom Atkins

22. Marlon Neocleous (28)

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

FWD/MID, 168cm

National Championships: 2 games, 16.0 disposals, 5.0 marks, 0.5 goals

It's been a strong finish to the season for Neocleous, who no doubt is a very different prospect to others around him. A natural goal sneak, he loves the ball in his hands up afield and is at his best with some space to execute in the forward half. He's an adept crumber and finisher in the forward 50, but lacks the pace to separate from opponents and doesn't have the tricks to exit congestion like some others.

Traits similar to: Jack Higgins

23. Jack Pickett (24)

Geelong Falcons/Vic Country

FWD, 194cm

Pickett was a top prospect throughout his bottom-age campaign. He's a traditional key forward that presents full-chested at the kicker and marks with arms outstretched. He's also a lovely set shot for goal, but is rehabilitating a torn ACL this year.

Traits similar to: Jye Amiss

24. Gabe Patterson (27)

Glenelg/South Australia

FWD, 184cm

National Championships: 4 games, 13.0 disposals, 2.5 tackles, 1.0 goals

After a tough championships it's been a truly brilliant second half of the season for Patterson. There's little doubt over the forward's impact with ball in hand, but finding enough of it has been a concern and showcasing his power and athleticism often enough has been something for Patterson to build towards. He's given recruiters something to think about towards the first round of the draft after blistering form in front of goals.

Traits similar to: Beau McCreery

25. Harvie Cooke (22)

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

MID/FWD, 176cm

National Championships: 4 games, 17.5 disposals, 7.0 marks, 1.0 goals

Cooke is 2026's Morrish Medallist for best and fairest in the Coates Talent League. It's well deserved for the midfielder's excellent season at the Knights where he was roving to Van Hattum and hitting the scoreboard regularly. Cooke was forced into forward roles at Metro where he was equally as damaging and showed he didn't need midfield minutes to create space for himself and hurt the opposition by foot.

Traits similar to: Sam Switkowski

26. Koby LeCras (26)

West Perth/Western Australia

FWD/MID, 192cm

A best on ground performance for the AFL Academy sits firmly in the minds for all draft watchers despite LeCras partially tearing his ACL and sitting out the rest of the year. The nephew of West Coast's Mark is a taller but equally creative half forward who can roam up onto a wing with his engine. He's clinical and efficient in his disposals.

Traits similar to: Ollie Dempsey

27. Jackson Phillips (-)

Dandenong Stingrays/Vic Country

MID, 182cm

National Championships: 4 games, 16.2 disposals, 3.8 marks, 3.2 tackles

Phillips's Stingrays are grand final bound, aided by his excellent midfield play. He offers impact with every possession, not collecting huge numbers but getting the ball in dangerous spots and regularly hitting the scoreboard. He likely doesn't exhibit the tools to be a bona fide inside midfielder at the next level but has positional versatility in his ball use and running power and could play off a wing or half forward.

Traits similar to: Justin McInerny

28. Toby Krasna (28)

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

MID, 181cm

National Championships: 3 games, 19.0 disposals, 3.3 marks, 1.0 goals

Krasna does his best work in transition where he finds space and excels kicking inside 50. He won't be a centre bounce midfielder at the next level without winning more of his own ball and averaged under one clearance per game for Vic Metro, but he's a standout prospect with the ball in the forward half.

Traits similar to: Jake Soligo

29. Keenan Boi (-)

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

FWD, 180cm

National Championships: 3 games, 13.3 disposals, 4.7 marks, 1.0 goals

Boi plays with rare physicality for junior football, bodylining the ball and man and exerting his authority with an edge. He's clean and executes under pressure when he needs to but brings his best traits forward without the ball where he tackles and pressures with the best of small forwards. He's primed for a big grand final on the weekend.

Traits similar to: Sam Powell-Pepper

30. George Dimer (23)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

FWD, 173cm

National Championships: 3 games, 16.0 disposals, 5.7 marks, 1.0 goals

Dimer is an intelligent small forward with the runs on the board for clubs to be confident that he won't be held back by his size. His performances for Haileybury in the APS were undeniable, plus he was one of Vic Metro's better forwards throughout the carnival despite not being a focal point in attack. He crumbs well, uses the ball smartly and creates opportunities for others.

Traits similar to: Hussien El Achkar

31. Albert MacGowan (-)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 187cm

National Championships: 4 games, 22.8 disposals, 6.2 marks, 1.0 tackles

One of the hottest players to finish the year has been MacGowan, who ended the year with a bang as the Dragons best performed player. He has operated with great success off a wing thanks to his aerial presence and skills, but has ambitions of becoming an inside midfielder if he can add ball-winning to his repertoire. MacGowan's knack of hitting the scoreboard with lovely set shots would be a nice penchant to transition to senior level.

Traits similar to: Matt Johnson

32. Marcus Prasad (-)

Dandenong Stingrays

FWD/MID, 167cm

Prasad is undersized and hasn't demonstrated midfield craft to the level you'd be confident projecting it. It's his forward half craft that makes him a national draft candidate, supremely gifted below his knees to the point he may be the cleanest player in the draft. Prasad gathers and swivels like lightning, though lacks penetration in his kick and doesn't hit the scoreboard to the regularity of other half forwards.

Traits similar to: Arthur Jones

33. Lochie Burrows (-)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

DEF/MID, 181cm

National Championships: 4 games, 13.0 disposals, 4.8 marks, 1.8 tackles

Burrows is brave and bold, with a blonde shock of hair you can't miss and endeavour at the coalface. He's played some of his best football as a hard-nosed midfielder with an appetite to tackle and pressure, but he appeals to clubs down back where he can lock down and intercept with good hands in the air.

Traits similar to: Max Michalanney

34. Benji Van Rooyen (30)

Claremont/Western Australia

RUC, 203cm

National Championships: 4 games, 14.0 disposals, 4.0 marks, 20.5 hitouts

Van Rooyen was the best performing ruck at the carnival, and deserves consideration higher than this mark. He showed off strong positioning behind the ball in open play to mop up for WA countless times and he doesn't overuse the ball. There's scope for Van Rooyen to play forward at his size but his ruck craft has steadily improved this year.

Traits similar to: Darcy Cameron

35. George Gale (29)

Claremont/Western Australia

MID, 190cm

National Championships: 4 games, 27.8 disposals, 5.2 marks, 2.8 tackles

Gale will play in a senior grand final this weekend after a stellar finish to the year. He burst into top 30 calculations with a strong showing at the carnival for WA and his power running through midfield is a feature. Gale could be an excellent wing at the next level with his positioning and strength lending himself to auxiliary roles, but he's also shown quality as an inside midfielder.

Traits similar to: Bo Allan

stories.headline: NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS urge action against threats from bettors
stories.summary: The NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS and their players' unions are urging state gambling regulators to combat escalating harassment and violent threats from sports bettors.
stories.body:
The five largest American professional sports leagues and their players' unions are urging state gambling regulators to combat escalating harassment and violent threats from sports bettors.

The NFL, NBA, Major League Baseball, NHL, Major League Soccer and their respective players' unions on Tuesday sent a letter to gambling regulators in 35 states and the District of Columbia, proposing a lifetime ban from legal sportsbooks for individuals who harass or threaten professional or amateur athletes, coaches, officials, team personnel or their families.

The leagues and unions want states to establish a streamlined reporting mechanism, allowing evidence of threats to be transmitted to regulators and law enforcement. Anyone found to have violated the policy would be placed on a sportsbook exclusion list shared among states.

"Too often, individuals who lose sports bets direct threatening and harassing messages toward players, coaches, and their families via social media and in-person interactions," the leagues' letter states. "Threatening the safety of an athlete or their family members over a sports bet crosses a bright ethical and criminal line, and it is entirely unacceptable."

In May 2025, pitcher Lance McCullers, then with the Houston Astros, said he received threats on social media to "find my kids and murder them" after a rough performance against the Cincinnati Reds. An investigation by Houston police determined an intoxicated bettor overseas was behind the threats.

Five states -- Louisiana, Massachusetts, Ohio, West Virginia and Wyoming -- already have similar policies in place, and some of the largest sportsbooks have taken steps to combat the issue. DraftKings and Fanatics partnered with Integrity Compliance 360 this summer to implement a technology that uses artificial intelligence and investigative tools to detect social media abuse and identify the people behind it.

"Threats and harassment in sports continue to escalate, threatening the safety of participants and the integrity of the ecosystem," Scott Sadin, co-founder and co-CEO of IC360, told ESPN. "True progress requires a unified response where leagues, operators, regulators and technology partners align around solutions to safeguard stakeholders across every touchpoint."

"It's just an infuriating issue," Matt King, CEO of Fanatics Betting and Gaming and a sports betting industry veteran, told ESPN in June.

Houston Rockets guard Fred VanVleet, president of the NBPA, said players are still adjusting to the new betting environment surrounding sports.

"We carry all of the burden, all of the risk and danger that comes with the association to gambling," VanVleet said in July. "It was one of those things that was just kind of thrown upon us, and I think everybody's trying to figure out how to adjust to it."

stories.headline: Warriors sell out Eden Park in 48 hours amid NRL's crowd woes
stories.summary: Hooker Sam Healey plans to draw inspiration from his rugby league idol to help him handle the pulsating atmosphere of a sold-out Eden Park.
stories.body:
Hooker Sam Healey plans to draw inspiration from his NRL idol to help him handle the pulsating atmosphere of a sold-out Eden Park.

The NRL announced that general-public tickets for Sunday's do-or-die semi-final between the Warriors and Newcastle in Auckland had sold out in less than 48 hours.

It comes after New Zealand were forced to relocate from their traditional home ground for the clash because Eden Park hosts about 25,000 more spectators than Go Media Stadium.

The 50,000-seat venue being full comes after the league was criticised over poor crowd numbers in the first week of finals, although the Warriors had a mostly sold-out attendance for their 26-16 loss to the Dolphins.

Regardless, it's the club's first clash at Eden Park since 2014, and will be a mammoth moment for New Zealand rugby league as the Warriors look to keep alive their hopes of a first premiership.

Healey is yet to play at the venue, but will be wanting to produce similar heroics to his idol Kevin Locke, who made a courageous try-saving tackle on Sydney Roosters centre Michael Jennings at the Fortress in 2013.

"I have played league since I was five or six or something like that, so I always loved the game," Healey said.

"I actually saw him (Locke) in the sheds the other day, and I said to my mum, 'Do you remember when he was my favourite player'. She just started laughing.

"He used to be my lock-screen on my phone ... I just said g'day."

Warriors back-rower Jacob Laban has only played once at the country's biggest sporting stadium.

"It was Kiwi A's versus Tonga A's, I think it was two, three years ago," he said.

"(After) New Zealand played Samoa (in the Pacific Championships) ... it was a pretty cool, good atmosphere.

"Obviously it (the crowd) is a little bit further (away) than Mt Smart, but it's not too bad. When you score a try, you can walk up to the fans over there, so it's still pretty close."

Laban won't be intimidated by the history of Eden Park, although the club has won only one of its six games at the venue.

The blond second-rower is intent on not just helping the Warriors set up a preliminary final against Penrith, but also on making his childhood self proud.

"I knew I wanted to play for the Warriors when I first heard about rugby league," Laban said.

"They came to Wellington. I don't know what year it was, but I still have this photo of me where I had half a Warriors face painted on and a Warriors T-shirt.

"I knew I wanted to play for the Warriors since I was young."
